chapter: Washington in the 1930s: big bands, lessons, first jobs
title: Chick Webb's band, and learning the front man was Bardu Ali
summary: He thinks Bardu Ali is Chick Webb, later learns Webb was the drummer, and finds he cannot yet pick out the band pianist.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Anyway, I liked that. So the next week, I found myself up there to hear Chick Webb. I heard Chick Webb's band, and I never will forget... I thought that the guy who was standing in front of the band was Chick Webb. And for a long time, it was quite a while, that somebody told me that the guy in front of the band wasn't Chick Webb; his name was Bardu Ali. At that particular time, all the bands had some character standing up there waving a stick in front of the band, and a lot of times it was not the bandleader who was doing it. In Chick Webb's case, he was the drummer in the and, and I also learned later that he had this physical disability that it wasn't convenient for him to come out on the stage. So Bardu Ali did all the MC'ing and the waving his hands in front of the band as the conductor.

I enjoyed listening to it. But there was so much going on, you didn't know where to really center your attention. At that particular time, I guess I was so I guess enchanted with everything that was going on on the stage, that I didn't settle in on any one instrumentalist. I always did try to

hear what the piano player was doing. But somehow, I couldn't hear the piano player, because I didn't know how to listen to him. He was playing the chords in the band, but the horns and everything were... My ears weren't that sensitive to actually center the piano player out. But I would watch him anyway. There were guys that had all sorts of ways of sitting sideways at the piano, and all sorts... Which was very interesting to me, you know.
